reason: The cited evidence (E1–E4) concerns different alloy systems (Nb-Si-Ti-based refractory alloys, parameter ranges for BC alloys, and a γ-γ' superalloy) and does not provide specific support for the oxidation mechanisms of the Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 FCC high-entropy alloy. None of the passages address Cr-rich scale formation, Ti-rich oxide spallation, or internal oxidation along grain boundaries in this alloy, leaving the key premises unsupported by the cited prior evidence.
premises: Cr and Ti in the alloy can form protective or disruptive oxide scales depending on atmosphere
Under oxidizing conditions, Cr forms a continuous passivating scale that later degrades via Ti-rich oxide formation and spallation
Under reducing conditions, a protective scale fails to form, enabling internal oxidation along grain boundaries
Internal oxidation depletes strengthening solutes and degrades local mechanical properties while preserving the FCC matrix
The cited evidence supports selective oxidation and scale adhesion behavior relevant to this alloy system
